Nora: FYI SAST flagged a HIGH in auth/graphql/resolvers.go in PR #9420: missing tenant scoping on `UpdateFeatureFlag` mutation. Also noticed calls to keystore.Sign() without audit attributes. Can we triage? :exclamation:
sec-bot: SAST run for PR #9420  2 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM. High: auth/graphql/resolvers.go: UpdateFeatureFlag - uses caller info but doesn't enforce tenant_id. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/scans/9420
Lee: can you paste the resolver snippet?
Nora: paste: ```go
// auth/graphql/resolvers.go
func (r *resolver) UpdateFeatureFlag(ctx context.Context, input FlagInput) (*Flag, error) {
  user := ctx.Value("user")
  // TODO: assumes request-level user -> applies flag globally if admin
  err := r.store.ApplyFlag(input.Name, input.Value)
  return r.store.GetFlag(input.Name), err
}
```
Brad: that looks like it applies the flag globally if user is admin. If the intent is per-tenant flags this is wrong. A malicious or mis-scoped admin could flip flags for other tenants.
Katie: KMS/keystore concern: I see `sig, _ := keystore.Sign(ctx, payload)` in the same flow. Our keystore expects Sign calls to include audit tags (actor/tenant/action) so posthoc tracing works. This call has no metadata wrapper.
Lee: immediate triage plan: 1) mark PR security-blocking; 2) enforce tenant scoping in resolver (derive tenant from ctx and pass to ApplyFlag); 3) wrap keystore.Sign with audit attrs; 4) add unit test to ensure UpdateFeatureFlag rejects cross-tenant attempts.
Nora: I'll put up a patch. Also noticed repo had an SAST suppression for graphql auth that was broad  I'll remove that suppression.
oncall-bot: Note: repo suppression removal scheduled by katie at 6555554310.
Brad: for keystore wrapper use: `ctx = keystore.WithAudit(ctx, map[string]string{"tenant_id": tid, "actor": uid, "action": "sign_flag"})` then call Sign. That will populate audit indices.
Katie: agree. Also propose adding a small linter rule to detect keystore.Sign/Decrypt/Encrypt calls without a WithAudit call in the same function scope. We can start with a grep-based CI check.
Lee: process ask: add a PR-template checkbox: "Touches auth/keystore/feature flags? Add security reviewer + tests + audit annotations." Small prompts reduce slips.
Nora: adding tests + linter in the patch. ETA 90m. Will ping when ready.
sec-bot: PR #9420 marked security-blocking by lee at 6555554335.
Brad: additional DAST note: the feature flag UI flow has an auth callback redirect; DAST found an open-redirect pattern if return_to is not validated. Recommend adding return_to allowlist and a DAST test in PR pipeline for auth endpoints.
Nora: good catch. I'll harden return_to and add an integration test.
Katie: runbook note: if a mis-scoped flag flip is detected in production, roll back flag change, audit keystore sign events for the actor and tenant, rotate signing key if unexplained signs occurred. Add this to sec-runbook/flag-misuse.md.
Lee: I'll open sec-workflows ticket to codify runbook and add the linter work item. Tagging @oncall for awareness.
oncall-bot: sec-workflows#1290 created: "Feature flag scoping + keystore audit enforcement" assigned to lee.
Nora: PR opened: https://git.redwood/internal/p/9421 - includes tenant enforcement, keystore.WithAudit, linter rule skeleton, and tests. Requesting review from lee/katie.
Brad: after merge, we should run a quick audit query: keystore.sign events in last 72h for feature-flag service and ensure tenant_id present; trigger rotation if not.
Katie: will add dashboard alert: if any keystore.Sign events missing tenant_id in 24h, page sec-oncall.
Nora: thanks folks  will follow up when CI passes. :thumbsup:
